**EatPoint 0.5.0**, a fork of [OpenNutriTracker](https://github.com/simonoppowa/OpenNutriTracker) that counts food in points: 1 point is 100 kcal of carbohydrate, protein or fat.

> **Preview build.** Installs as its own app (`io.github.grohle.eatpoint`), not on Google Play or the App Store yet. It updates 0.4.x builds in place, keeping your data, and the app offers it by itself.

## What's new in 0.5

**Household units you can trust**
- Every household unit ("2 tortillas", "5 lonchas") was checked: the everyday-food catalogue against Spanish supermarket packs and household-measure tables, and the downloadable database food by food (about 4,700 foods).
- A wheat tortilla is now 40 g (it was matched wrongly), and "tortilla de patatas", pita bread, burger buns, sausages, burgers, sliced turkey or chicken, nuggets, croissants, cereal bars and more have their own units.
- Foods without a natural unit (juices, sauces, flours, chips, loose foods) no longer show one; "zumo de naranja" is not "1 orange".
- The food database updates to version 2 (Settings → Food database).

**Your own weight per unit**
- Tap the unit under a food in the meal editor, or "Weight per unit" when logging, and say what one weighs for you. It's used everywhere: logging, menus and the shopping list.

**My foods**
- A food editor in You → My foods (and in Food database): your foods and the whole database in one search. Create new foods, edit any food and keep it as yours, set its weight per unit, delete your own.

**Backup**
- Settings → Backup (also in Share and sync): one file with everything, saved on the phone, sent to Google Drive, Dropbox or any app, or copied straight to Google Drive, now or automatically every day or week (the latest 10 are kept). Restore from a file or from Drive. Earlier EatPoint exports restore too.

## Downloads
- `EatPoint-0.5.0-arm64-v8a.apk`: for almost every phone from the last few years.
- `EatPoint-0.5.0-armeabi-v7a.apk`: for older 32-bit phones (Android 8.0+).
